text:
maya: Heads-up: Postmortem draft for yesterday's vendor token-throttle incident is up. Short summary: cloud-auth provider applied a dynamic rate-limiter during a regional surge; our token refresh pattern caused bursts and ~12% of model-registry calls to fail under load.

sahil: Ugh. Do we have a concrete mitigation plan or temporary knobs?

ellie: I started a playbook fragment in the doc: add synthetic token probe, soft-rate-limit client-side, and bump token TTL if vendor allows. Also propose an automated fallback to cached credentials for 30s.

maya: Good. Can we assign owners + realistic timelines? This is recurring pattern across auth providers.

ellie: I'll own the runbook and alerting changes (synthetic probe + dashboard). ETA: 2025-03-07. Tasks: add probe, new Grafana panels, and a paging rule for >5% token-error rate over 3m.

kyle: I'll take client-library changes (exponential backoff + jitter, local short-term token cache). PR planned by 2025-03-05, rollout canary to Dedicated first.

james: I'll handle vendor coordination—ask for documented burst limits and request a sandbox for load testing. Target: vendor reply + limits doc by 2025-03-06.

maya: Action list consolidated here (copying into issues):
- A1 runbook & probes -> owner: ellie -> due: 2025-03-07
- A2 client lib backoff & cache -> owner: kyle -> due: 2025-03-05
- A3 vendor SLA/limits doc -> owner: james -> due: 2025-03-06
- A4 dashboard + alert -> owner: ellie -> due: 2025-03-07
- A5 canary rollout plan -> owner: kyle -> due: 2025-03-09
- A6 retro + quarterly recurrence watch -> owner: maya -> schedule: 2025-03-10

sahil: For A4, can we add an anomaly detector for token-exchange latency spikes (not just error rate)? Those preceded failures.

ellie: yes. Plan: token-exchange p50/p95/p99 + sudden delta alert. Will add to dashboard.

maya: Also adding instrumentation: emit vendor-quota headers into our tracing span so we can correlate X-RateLimit-* to failures.

kyle: Note on rollout: client change will include a feature flag and a short TTL override in config for quick revert. Example config snippet:
```yaml
auth_client:
  backoff_strategy: exp_jitter
  max_backoff_ms: 2000
  local_cache_ttl_s: 30
```

ops-bot: Reminder: retro scheduled: Mon 2025-03-10 11:00am PT in #incidents. Invitees: maya, sahil, ellie, kyle, james, platform-eng.

deploy-bot: Runbook change committed: /docs/runbooks/vendor-token-throttle.md (PR #2047) by ellie.

maya: One more thing — this is a class of "burst-refresh" recurrence. Proposal: a lightweight quarterly drill where we test token refresh traffic patterns in a controlled Dedicated burst to catch regressions. who volunteers to own the drill program?

sahil: I'll take the drill program coordination. Suggest we add it as a recurring task in the runbook with test plan and KPIs.

ellie: Adding test plan skeleton to the runbook now (probe scenarios, load profile, expected metrics).

maya: Great. Follow-ups: please open the issues tonight and link them from the postmortem doc. I'll verify owners and close the loop in the retro. :thumbsup:

kyle: Will open A2 + A5 issues and tag @sahil for drill schedule.

james: Reached out to vendor account rep, asked for limits doc and sandbox access. I'll update here when they respond.

maya: Thanks everyone — this one looks actionable. We'll treat the vendor token-throttle as a high-priority cross-team remediation until A1-A5 are complete.

(END)
